item.title: Celtic vs Motherwell: Scottish Premiership Title Race Heats Up in Crucial Clash
item.description:
Can Celtic afford another slip-up? With nine games left and a five-point deficit to league leaders Hearts, every match is now a must-win for the Bhoys.

Quick Summary: Celtic host Motherwell at Celtic Park in a Scottish Premiership clash with major title implications. Martin O’Neill’s side sit second, five points behind Hearts, while Motherwell — managed by Celtic-linked Jens Berthel Askou — are fourth, 10 points off the pace. Celtic are unbeaten in eight of their last nine league games under O’Neill’s second interim spell, but Motherwell already beat them 2-0 in December.

item.title: Jeremy Fears Jr. All-American: Michigan State's Record-Chasing Point Guard
item.description:
Jeremy Fears Jr. is 27 assists away from rewriting Michigan State basketball history. The redshirt sophomore point guard has turned a season that began with questions into one that has produced All-American recognition, a Big Ten First Team selection, and a legitimate shot at breaking Cassius Winston’s single-season assist record – one of the most revered marks in Spartan lore.

At 15.5 points and 9.1 assists per game, Fears has established himself as one of the most productive floor generals in all of college basketball. His 264 assists on the season lead the Big Ten, and the record of 291 set by Winston – now an NBA veteran – is firmly within reach.

item.title: Randy Orton Turns Heel: Viper Bloodies Cody Rhodes in Shocking WrestleMania 42 Contract Signing
item.description:
There is something uniquely chilling about watching a friendship die on live television. On the March 13 episode of WWE SmackDown, Randy Orton did exactly what millions of fans feared and many more secretly hoped for – he turned on Cody Rhodes during the WrestleMania 42 contract signing, leaving the American Nightmare bloodied in the ring.

The attack was sudden, methodical, and unmistakably Orton at his most dangerous. Just like that, the Viper shed his skin and reminded the wrestling world why he has been one of the most feared competitors in WWE history for over two decades.

item.title: Ohio State vs Michigan Basketball: Can the 8th-Seed Buckeyes Shock the Big Ten's Best?
item.description:
The stage is set for one of college basketball’s fiercest rivalries to take center court in Chicago. Ohio State, the 8th seed, will square off against top-seeded Michigan in the Big Ten Tournament quarterfinals on March 13, 2026, at the United Center, with tipoff scheduled for noon ET on Big Ten Network.

Michigan enters with a staggering 29-2 record and a 19-1 mark in Big Ten play, while Ohio State (21-11) had to claw past Iowa just to earn this matchup. The question everyone is asking: does Ohio State have any realistic path to an upset, or is Michigan simply too dominant?

item.title: Spencer Jones Optioned: Why the Yankees' Top Prospect Is Headed to Triple-A
item.description:
Spencer Jones homered. Spencer Jones impressed. And then Spencer Jones was sent to minor league camp anyway. The New York Yankees’ decision to option one of their most exciting young talents to Triple-A, despite a standout spring training performance, has become one of the most talked-about storylines heading into the 2026 MLB season.

Key Takeaways:

  • Spencer Jones was reassigned to minor league camp on Monday, March 9
  • Jones homered alongside Jasson Dominguez in a Yankees win over the Phillies on March 10
  • The Yankees’ deep outfield roster left no room for Jones on the Opening Day squad
  • Jones has drawn comparisons to Shohei Ohtani for his blend of size, power, and athleticism
  • Both Jones and Jasson Dominguez are expected to begin the season in the minors

A Spring to Remember, Then a Trip Down

Spencer Jones turned heads throughout spring training in 2026. The towering outfield prospect showcased the raw power and athleticism that made him one of the Yankees’ most coveted young players, and he punctuated his Grapefruit League stint with a home run in a Yankees victory over the Philadelphia Phillies at Clearwater on March 10.

item.title: Utah Mammoth Lock In Nick Schmaltz with Massive $64 Million Extension
item.description:
The Utah Mammoth just made one of the biggest moves of the NHL season, and it signals exactly where this franchise is headed. By locking in Nick Schmaltz to an eight-year, $64 million contract extension, the Mammoth have removed one of the league’s top pending free agents from the open market and planted a flag for long-term competitiveness in Salt Lake City.

Key Takeaways:

  • Nick Schmaltz signs an 8-year extension worth $64 million ($8 million AAV)
  • The Mammoth hold 73 points through 65 games in their second season since relocating from Arizona
  • GM Bill Armstrong continues an aggressive roster-building approach
  • Utah plans to be aggressive in the summer trade market, particularly targeting centers
  • Defenseman Mikhail Sergachev returns to the lineup after missing over a week

The Schmaltz Deal: Breaking Down the Numbers

The contract, announced on Wednesday, March 11, carries a cap hit of $8.0 million per season over eight years. For a forward who was set to become an unrestricted free agent this summer, the deal represents a significant commitment from both sides.

item.title: Jaquan Brisker Free Agency: Where Will the Former Bears Safety Land?
item.description:
Jaquan Brisker Remains One of the Best Players Still Available in Free Agency

The first wave of 2026 NFL free agency has come and gone, and one name keeps surfacing in trade rumors and landing-spot speculation: Jaquan Brisker. The hard-hitting safety spent the first four years of his career with the Chicago Bears, but the relationship appears to be over. With the Bears pivoting to other options and multiple contenders circling, Brisker’s next move could reshape a secondary across the league.

item.title: Jacob Martin Signs with Titans: $11M Deal Reunites Edge Rusher with Robert Saleh
item.description:
Jacob Martin Cashes In: Titans Land Edge Rusher on Two-Year Deal

The Tennessee Titans continue their aggressive 2026 free agency spending spree. On March 12, the team agreed to sign outside linebacker Jacob Martin to a two-year deal worth up to $11 million, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz.

The signing reunites Martin with Titans head coach Robert Saleh, who previously coached him during their time together with the New York Jets in 2022.

item.title: Kawhi Leonard Fuels Clippers' Stunning Turnaround After Disastrous Start
item.description:
Few players in NBA history have carried a team from the edge of irrelevance back into the playoff picture the way Kawhi Leonard is doing right now. After the LA Clippers lost 21 of their first 27 games this season, most analysts had already written their obituary. Leonard had other plans.

Key Takeaways

  • Kawhi Leonard is averaging 28.0 points, 6.4 rebounds, 3.7 assists, and 2.0 steals per game on elite shooting splits
  • The Clippers clawed back from a 6-21 start to reach .500 at 32-32, surpassing the Warriors for 8th in the Western Conference
  • An NBA investigation into a $28 million endorsement deal with Aspiration has raised salary cap circumvention questions
  • Despite the turnaround, Leonard insists there is “nothing to be happy about” — the job is far from finished

Kawhi Leonard’s Monster Season by the Numbers

Leonard’s individual performance this season has been nothing short of extraordinary. At 34 years old, the two-time Finals MVP is putting up numbers that rival his peak seasons in San Antonio and Toronto.

item.title: Knicks vs Jazz Breakdown: Karl-Anthony Towns Dominates as New York Eyes Eastern Conference Surge
item.description:
Nobody in the NBA is collecting double-doubles faster than Karl-Anthony Towns right now, and the Utah Jazz are about to find out why.

The New York Knicks enter their March 11 matchup against the Utah Jazz riding a wave of momentum as one of the most dangerous teams in the Eastern Conference. At 41-25, they sit firmly in third place, while Utah limps into Madison Square Garden with a brutal 20-45 record near the bottom of the Western Conference. The last time these two teams met? The Knicks obliterated them 146-112 in December.

item.title: WVU Basketball Big 12 Tournament: Mountaineers' NCAA Hopes on the Line
item.description:
WVU basketball needs a miracle run — and they know it. The seventh-seeded West Virginia Mountaineers enter the Big 12 Tournament at 18-13, sitting firmly on the outside of the NCAA Tournament bubble. Their only path to March Madness likely runs through Kansas City.

Key Takeaways

  • WVU enters the Big 12 Tournament as the 7th seed with an 18-13 record
  • The Mountaineers are off Joe Lunardi’s NCAA Tournament bubble
  • Key wins this season: Kansas, BYU, and Pitt (71-49)
  • Senior guard Honor Huff earned All-Big 12 Honorable Mention
  • WVU women’s basketball won the Big 12 title and may host NCAA games

WVU Basketball’s Roller-Coaster Season Under Ross Hodge

First-year head coach Ross Hodge has navigated a season full of extremes. The highs have been exhilarating — none more than a 71-49 demolition of rival Pitt that Hodge says he’ll “never forget for as long as I live.”

item.title: Kai Havertz Haunts Former Club: Arsenal's Penalty Hero Secures 1-1 Draw at Leverkusen
item.description:
Kai Havertz stepped up when it mattered most. Returning to the BayArena where his career began, the 26-year-old Arsenal forward converted a late penalty to secure a crucial 1-1 draw against Bayer Leverkusen in the Champions League Round of 16 first leg.

Key Takeaways

  • Bayer Leverkusen 1-1 Arsenal — Kai Havertz scored a late penalty to level for the Gunners
  • Robert Andrich headed Leverkusen ahead from a corner kick
  • Noni Madueke won the penalty after being fouled by Malik Tillman in the 87th minute
  • Havertz made just his 10th appearance of the season after two surgeries in seven months
  • Arsenal won all 8 league phase matches — the only team with a perfect record

item.title: Trey Hendrickson Injury Update: How a Core Muscle Surgery Is Reshaping NFL Free Agency
item.description:
The most dominant pass rusher of the last three NFL seasons is sitting at home without a team, and a single surgery is the reason why.

Trey Hendrickson, the four-time Pro Bowl defensive end, entered 2026 free agency expecting a bidding war. Instead, he got silence, lowball offers, and a gap between his asking price and reality that could be as wide as $10 million per year. The culprit? A core muscle injury that cut his 2025 season to just seven games and forced him under the knife in December.
